What is measured

For each output the wallet holds 36 bytes: a 32-byte curve point and the first 4 bytes of the ciphertext. The test is:

  • unpack the point (a division and a square root),
  • multiply it by the wallet's secret key,
  • hash the result into a key, then hash that key to get the expected first ciphertext value,
  • compare 4 bytes.

Notes:

  • The test data is 4,096 ciphertexts made with the Midnight ledger's own code (v2.1.101), repeated to reach the chosen count. Every result is compared with the value the ledger computed.
  • GPU runs process the whole chosen count, in batches of up to 65,536. The time includes sending data to the GPU and reading results back; shader compilation is reported separately.
  • CPU runs use the ledger's code compiled to WebAssembly. They run for about five seconds and the rate is projected to the chosen count.
  • The GPU version does not do the ledger's subgroup check on the point. CPU runs skip it too unless the box is ticked.
